title: Bounded shift run
statement: Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $mode$ be Boolean, let $o$ be an oracle assigning a Boolean value to each of five indices and each Boolean word, let $y$ be a Boolean word, and let $st$ be a state of fifteen natural-number registers. Suppose every register of $st$ is at most $B$, its shift scratch register is zero, and the register selected by the shift operation $k$, multiplied by $2^{c}$ where $c$ is the loop-counter register of $st$, is at most $B$. Then the register program has a finite run from phase zero of shift operation $k$ with register values $st$ to its exit phase, with the loop-counter register cleared and the selected register replaced by its original value times $2^{c}$; all other registers retain their original values. The guard holds at every configuration before the endpoint.

Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let the mode be Boolean, let $o$ be an oracle
assigning a Boolean answer to each of five indices and binary words, and let $y$ be a
binary word. Suppose a register state $st$ has each of its fifteen coordinates at most
$B$, its scratch register $z$ is zero, and the coordinate selected by the shift
operation $k$, multiplied by $2^c$, is at most $B$. Then the specified register program
has a finite run, guarded at every configuration before its endpoint, from phase zero of
shift operation $k$ with registers $st$ to the exit phase of $k$, with the counter
register cleared and the selected coordinate replaced by its original value times $2^c$;
